text: Antarctica is the driest continent on Earth. Parts of it have not received rain in over two million years. Surprisingly, it is classified as a desert because it receives so little annual precipitation.

Elephants communicate using rumbles pitched too low for humans to hear. These infrasonic calls travel for miles through the ground, and other elephants detect them through their feet. A herd can coordinate its movements across vast distances this way.

Golf has been played on the moon. In nineteen seventy-one, astronaut Alan Shepard smuggled a club head aboard Apollo Fourteen and hit two balls. In the weak lunar gravity, he joked that the second one flew for miles and miles.

In parts of Southeast Asia, thousands of fireflies flash in perfect unison, lighting entire riverbanks like blinking holiday displays. Scientists studied the synchrony for decades, and the underlying math now helps explain heart cells and power grids.

More people have been to the moon than have reached the deepest point of the ocean. Twelve astronauts walked on the lunar surface, while only three people have descended to the bottom of the Mariana Trench.

Painting the Golden Gate Bridge is a job that never ends. Crews continuously touch up its famous International Orange coating to fight salt-air corrosion. The color itself was originally just a primer that the architect decided to keep.

The Arctic tern makes the longest migration of any animal, flying from the Arctic to Antarctica and back every year. Over its lifetime, one bird may cover one and a half million miles, equal to three round trips to the moon.

The longest hiccuping spree ever recorded lasted sixty-eight years. Charles Osborne of Iowa started hiccuping in nineteen twenty-two and did not stop until nineteen ninety. He hiccuped approximately four hundred thirty million times.

The marathon's odd distance of twenty-six point two miles exists because of British royalty. The nineteen oh eight London course was extended so the race could start beneath the windows of Windsor Castle and finish in front of the royal box.

Your liver can regrow to full size from as little as a quarter of its original tissue. It is the only human organ with this ability, and a living donor's liver typically regenerates within just a few months.
